_comment: Structural exceptions for sbsi-docx-format-core's validator/normalizer, discovered by inspecting this template's actual OOXML (word/document.xml, word/styles.xml). Every value below is the engine's own generic default — listed explicitly so future template registrations have a concrete example to copy and edit, and so a reviewer can see at a glance what was verified against the real file rather than assumed.
_cover_page_strategy_note: Verified: paragraph 'Số: .../QĐ-TGĐ, Hà Nội, ngày...' (the promulgation-page opener) has <w:pageBreakBefore/>, immediately after the cover + doc-info table + TOC on page 1. Everything before it is excluded from ordinary-text/numbering checks.
_appendix_heading_pattern_note: Verified: 'Phụ lục số: NN' paragraphs mark each appendix (Danh mục tài liệu tham khảo uses manually-numbered '1. ... 2. ...' legal citations with no numPr — tolerated as a WARNING, not blocking, inside this zone).
_structural_heading_patterns_note: No additions needed: this template's real hierarchy uses paragraph styles 'Style1' (outline level 0, auto-numbered 'Chương %1' via its own numbering definition) and 'Style2' (outline level 1, auto-numbered 'Điều %1.' via numId 19) — both real Word outline levels, so the engine's generic default Chương/Điều text-pattern check correctly never fires as a false positive here (there is no bold-Normal text mimicking that vocabulary in this template).
_known_style_hierarchy_note: Informational only (not read by the scripts) — for a human/agent registering a future template to see a worked example of how to record a template's actual style-to-outline-level mapping instead of assuming 'Chương/Điều' literal style names.
_toc_field_switches_note: Informational: confirms the TOC field is outline-level-driven (levels 1-3), consistent with Style1/Style2 mapping to outline 0/1.
known_rendering_caveat: LibreOffice (used by render_qa.py) did not clearly honor this template's paragraph-level 'numPr numId="0"' override on the Style1 heading the same way Word does during manual verification — treat render_qa.py's PDF/PNG output as a strong visual-QA proxy, not a guaranteed Word-identical render. Confirm final numbering appearance in real Word before high-stakes distribution.
